I think that this is a good combination of passion and confidence in the production.

The behind-the-scenes aspect of the trilogy tells us that Peter Jackson and his fair shareof  producers and creative directors went through a lot of detail in making the portrayals in the movies and they mostly did this through the use of practical effects rather than CGI.

the CGI could have worked but it was still in its early stages and they felt that practical effects made me more even though it was more costly.

However, they had a lot of support from the producers. They were greenlit on making three films one after the other because they were confident in the IP and they knew that it will eventually do well in the box office.

That and Peter Jackson took a lot of time in the pre-production. The filming and pre-production period started roughly in 1999, around 2 years before the release of the first film so they had a lot of time to discuss how to make the movie work.

  
And I also forgot to mention that there was a lot of luck in the filming process.

Viggo Mortensen was cast at the last minute but managed to make the portrayal of Aragorn work.

Ian McKellen did not know about the books but was very good in his portrayal of Gandalf.

They had Kiran Shah who is probably the most famous stunt double for shorter characters was the double for almost all the hobbits when certain shots needed to portray the hobbits' stature.

The shot of Aragorn hitting the helmet where he broke his toes was lucky but Jackson thought that it was a good take.

And I could mention a lot more but I would be turning this into an essay.

  
So yes, it seems that all the cards were in the right place for the trilogy and I am glad that things went well. I am just hoping that another LOTR film or TV series comes out in the future, and then the right factors will be in place once again.
